cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I withdrew my college application. Have you told Mum? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked. I said my sister's plans were hers to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then there's more. I've leased a bakery. Can I send you the address?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Call me. Mum uses my tablet; she'd see the message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. I'll call. It's Mum's old bakery. I want you there when I tell her.

mechanism: A directs a family disclosure plan and releases deeper business details after B proves discretion, accepting a safer communication method and inviting B into the final disclosure.
confusable: Unlike telling all secrets at once, A escalates from college withdrawal to bakery lease to family significance after B responses; authority adapts channel to keep trusted help.
comparison: Family legacy and a shared tablet differ from club staffing plans and gossip about replacements.
seedUse: D131-b protected college plans, bakery lease and Mum old bakery; S02-a changes the contact method around B warning.
